fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. "How long" points to a wait that has already been going on. Habakkuk says he has been calling for help and crying out. The words themselves suggest it's been a while.

You've got it, friend. Habakkuk says, “For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.” That's the reason he gives for why justice comes out twisted. Notice he doesn't blame bad luck. He points straight at the wicked.
That's the opposite, friend. The LORD calls it a work you "…would never believe even if someone told you." If everyone saw it coming, it wouldn't be astounding. He even says, “…be utterly astounded!”
That's the one, friend. The LORD says they march “…to seize dwellings not their own.” They march across the earth to take places that belong to others. It's a hard picture.
Not quite, baker. The text says nothing about land they once owned. It says they march “…to seize dwellings not their own.” That's the reason the LORD gives.
Yes, friend. The LORD says, “from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.” Their idea of justice comes from the Chaldeans themselves.
This one's true, friend, so let's look at the verse. The LORD says, “from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.” Their justice comes from themselves, just as the statement says.
That's backwards on the slow part, friend. The verse says the horses are “…swifter than leopards…” Swifter means faster, so slow doesn't fit.
That's it, friend. “They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.” The picture is a vulture swooping down on its prey. The LORD is showing how they come at their target.

That's right, baker. The statement is false because the Chaldeans “…laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.” A strong fortress doesn't make them turn back. They build siege ramps to seize it.
Not this one, baker. The verse says they scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. Those rulers aren't what the LORD names as their god. The verse says, “their own strength is their god.”
